name: gsply
reason: The pinned 0.4.6 plyread(path) API rejected the valid ordinary ASCII PLY triangle as an unsupported Gaussian Splatting PLY. A separate valid ASCII splat control was not established, so its narrower ASCII coverage is unknown.

name: mdal
reason: The 1.1.0 project documents a Stanford PLY ASCII Mesh driver, but its source build failed because native MDAL headers and library were absent. No runnable control result was established.

name: pylmesh
reason: The project documents ASCII PLY import through load_mesh(path), but version 0.1.3 has no macOS wheel and its source build was not attempted in this batch.

name: fury
reason: Older official documentation documents io.load_polydata(path) for PLY, while the reviewed 2.1.0 reference no longer lists that function. An exact current local API and valid-control result remain unestablished.

name: spectra3D
reason: The project documents read_ply(path) for a specialized spectral PLY, but release license evidence and a valid-control result were not established.

name: ply3d
reason: The summary says it handles PLY 3D geometries, but no documented exact local input API or valid-control result was established.

name: open3d-cpu
reason: This Open3D distribution has no matching macOS ARM wheel in the reviewed release; it was not built or tested here. It would share the Open3D parser family if verified.

name: pyply
reason: Its project description says it is functional data manipulation inspired by R, not a Polygon File Format input API.

name: ply
reason: This distribution is Python Lex & Yacc; PLY is its name, not the 3D file format it parses.

name: plydata
reason: It implements dplyr-like DataFrame operations, not a Polygon File Format reader.

name: mesh-reducer
reason: Pinned 2.0.2 load_mesh(path, clusters=1) raised a Rust PanicException on the valid ASCII triangle after reporting the standard vertex_indices face property as unexpected. It produced no correct parse result on this control.

name: meshlib
reason: The publisher explicitly calls MeshLib source-available and restricts commercial use. It does not meet this collection's open-source release requirement.

name: pointcloudlib
reason: The reviewed package documents depth estimation and 3D modeling, but no exact PLY input API. Its import also failed because the published dependency list omitted transformers.

name: ply-visualizer
reason: The reviewed Python package exposes viewer/session APIs that hand files to its browser engine; no Python library API returning observable PLY vertices or faces was established.
